correctness.rationale: The cover Y_n:w²=t^(2n)+1 is smooth since p∤n; the tame involution t->t^-1,w->w/t^n has quotient X_n with invariant differentials eta_i=omega_i-omega_(n-i). For each i=1..n-1, hyperelliptic Cartier coefficients of (t^(2n)+1)^((p-1)/2) are nonzero binomial terms iff the least residue r_i=pi mod 2n lies in 1..n-1, in which case i maps to one distinct output. Under p²=-1 mod2n, theta(i)=min(r_i,2n-r_i) is a fixed-point-free involution on 1..n-1 switching active and inactive indices; i and n-i have equal activity, hence exactly (n-1)/4 active invariant pairs. This also forces n=1 mod4. Iterating transitions multiplies i by p²=-1, outside active index range, giving C²=0, and rank g/2 implies imC=kerC. Smoothness, genus g=(n-1)/2 and a=g-rank are consistent. Independent modular calculations of Cartier rank and square zero for 6 admissible (p,n) pairs confirm, but infinite proof is the residue involution.

value.rationale: The Jacobian a-number measures local p-torsion and is not determined by supersingular Newton slopes, maximum point count, or rational Jacobian group abstract structure. Uniform half-rank computation for a natural maximal low-automorphism curve family, with explicit genus-six cases in infinitely many characteristics, is a motivated exact geometric invariant.

final_claim: For odd n>5, p>3 with p²=-1 mod 2n, the Dickson quotient X_n:y²=(x+2)D_n(x) has Cartier rank and a-number (n-1)/4, C²=0 and imC=kerC; maximality and two-element automorphisms are previously known.
